carried_on.headline: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
carried_on.summary: China’s espionage agency has been running a secret campaign to help the country’s companies acquire advanced A.I. chips and to gather intelligence on the sector, officials say.
carried_on.author: Chris Buckley and Julian E. Barnes

carried_on.headline: Drones, Texts and Diversions: How Mexico Captured a Most Wanted Man
carried_on.summary: U.S. and Mexican authorities shared intelligence for weeks to track Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a drug cartel leader that a U.S. official called the most dangerous man in Mexico.
carried_on.author: Steve Fisher, Paulina Villegas and Alan Feuer

carried_on.headline: Looking for the Formula to Stop an Apocalypse
carried_on.summary: Mike Winer and his colleagues are trying to build a mathematical safeguard to keep A.I. under human control. They fear they are running out of time.
carried_on.author: Eli Saslow and Erin Schaff

carried_on.headline: Republicans Debate Why They Lost the Midterms, and if Trump Is to Blame
carried_on.summary: A divide is emerging in the party over what caused its wipeout midterm defeats, foreshadowing a battle over how to move forward before 2028.
carried_on.author: Bayliss Wagner

carried_on.headline: Is Annie Andrews Too Real for the Senate? South Carolinians Are About to Find Out.
carried_on.summary: The pediatrician, who once compared JD Vance to the herpes virus, notched one of the most shocking upsets of the midterm elections by defeating Senator Darline Graham.
carried_on.author: Emily Davies
